tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with 'Use this skill when someone asks whether Amazon DynamoDB is why their application is slow' — imperative phrasing framed as an instruction to the agent. It lists multiple explicit trigger contexts (high/spiky p99, alarm fired, intermittent timeouts, slow first call, flat dashboard but slow writes, pre-peak review, cross-operation/table comparison) covering user intent rather than internal mechanics, and it is a single concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when someone asks whether Amazon DynamoDB is why their application is slow — a table shows high or spiky p99 or average latency, a SuccessfulRequestLatency alarm fired, requests intermittently time out, the first call after idle is slow, or the latency dashboard looks flat while users still see slow writes."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on DynamoDB-specific domain knowledge (what SuccessfulRequestLatency does and doesn't measure, outcome rules, input parsing rules) and never explains generic concepts like what CloudWatch or an API is. Every paragraph conveys non-obvious, skill-specific facts.
tests.evidence: "SuccessfulRequestLatency measures time internal to the DynamoDB service — client activity and network trip times are excluded — and only for successful requests..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (exact queries, thresholds, report templates) is kept in references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body. The Outcomes table and Critical Rules present concise decision criteria, not exhaustive lookup tables.
tests.evidence: "[references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md) — load before the first API call. The exact read-only queries and the dimensions..."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All four files in references/ are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear statement of when to load it (before first API call, after collection before classifying, before writing the report, before explaining mechanisms).

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ without absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile parts (input validation rejection rules, workflow order, critical rules on read-only operations) are stated as exact, non-negotiable instructions, while judgment-requiring parts (classification, contributing factors, hypothesis framing) are explained with rationale rather than rigid scripts, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "READ ONLY. Only the operations in the data-collection allowlist... this skill never reads item data." vs. "An elevated p50 shows DynamoDB processing time rose, not why... present them as hypotheses unless a collected metric supports one."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal menu options; it specifies a single primary tool (use_aws) and clear single-path classification logic.
tests.evidence: "Data is acquired with the agent's native use_aws tool under the assumed role in the target account."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (parse input, collect, classify, apply contributing factors, validate) applicable to any table/operation, not a one-off instance; specific output templates and outcome IDs are details within a reusable approach.
tests.evidence: "Copy this checklist into your working notes and tick each item as it completes... 1. Parse and validate input... 5. Classify..."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated section documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain, such as the trap of empty error series and flat curves hiding throttling.
tests.evidence: "An empty error or throttle series is not automatically zero... Otherwise it is NoData — unknown — and it blocks LT-05." and "A flat curve beside throttle events is consistent with retry-inflated client latency..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report, and a dedicated reference file (report-format.md) is explicitly designated to hold the output template, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: "[references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) — load before writing the report. Structure, recommended-action preconditions, health rating, and the pre-render validation checks."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.evidence: No inline template of significant length appears in the body; templates are deferred to "[references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md)".
